## 📉 Where the GDPR budget really goes


The audit-style fee people expect does not exist for GDPR. The spend is ongoing: knowing where personal data lives, keeping your[Record of Processing Activities (RoPA)](https://www.strac.io/blog/ropa-template) current, answering DSARs on time, and proving Article 32 security. Those recurring tasks, not a one-off exam, are what make GDPR expensive, and they are the parts a data-security platform automates.

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs: GDPR compliance cost


### How much does GDPR compliance cost in 2026?


GDPR compliance cost ranges from about $10,000 for a small company doing it leanly to $100,000 or more for a mid-size enterprise, driven by a DPO or consultant, data mapping and RoPA, DSAR tooling, Article 32 security controls, and legal work. The ongoing data-mapping, RoPA, and DSAR work is where Strac removes most of the recurring cost.


### Is there an official GDPR certification?


No. Unlike SOC 2 or ISO 27001, there is no single official GDPR certificate you buy. GDPR is a regulation you demonstrate compliance with through records (like a RoPA), security controls, and DSAR processes. That is why most GDPR cost is tooling and staff time, not an exam fee.


### What is the most expensive part of GDPR compliance?


For most teams it is the ongoing data work: finding where personal data lives, keeping a Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) current, and fulfilling data subject access requests. Strac automates all three with sensitive data discovery across SaaS, cloud, and endpoints, which is why it cuts the recurring GDPR bill.


### How does Strac reduce GDPR compliance cost?


Strac is a data-security platform (DSPM and DLP). It discovers and classifies personal data automatically, keeps your data inventory and RoPA current, and pinpoints where a subject's data sits for DSARs. Strac Comply then automates the ISO 27001 security program that satisfies GDPR Article 32, from $4,995 per year. Strac is not a GDPR certification product, because none exists.


### Do I need a Data Protection Officer?


Only some organizations must appoint a DPO (for example, large-scale monitoring or special-category processing). Many use a fractional DPO or consultant for roughly $10,000 or more per year. The DPO cost is separate from the tooling and security costs Strac addresses.
